record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can stable self-similar weakly localized solutions for dispersive or hyperbolic wave equations be constructed in dimensions below five, and can one prove in such dimensions that relevant solutions decompose into a free wave plus a weakly localized part rather than collapsing to a purely localized state? The setting includes mass-critical behavior, possible saturation of nonlinearities, and the need to determine whether such solutions have physical significance and whether they undermine the inverse-scattering principle that asymptotic data determine the system.

evidence.quote: While the current method of construction applies only in five or more dimensions, it is anticipated that similar results hold in any dimension. In any dimension, the mass-critical equation possesses a self-similar solution. One must properly saturate the nonlinearity to obtain a stable solution. The decomposition into a free wave and a weakly localized part remains valid, at least in three dimensions and higher (in the spherically symmetric case). However, one must demonstrate that certain solutions do not collapse to a purely localized form. It may be simpler to generate more examples by considering systems of equations. The physical significance of such solutions hinges on the type of models exhibiting such behavior. This also raises questions about the validity of the Inverse Scattering Meta-Theorem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider mass-critical dispersive or hyperbolic nonlinear wave equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for example, the mass-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation $i\partial_t u + \Delta u = \pm |u|^{4/d} u$, the mass-critical generalized KdV, or analogous nonlinear wave/Klein–Gordon models), possibly with a saturation of the nonlinearity (i.e. replacing the pure power $|u|^{4/d}u$ by a smooth nonlinearity that agrees with $|u|^{4/d}u$ for small amplitudes and is bounded or sub-critical for large amplitudes). A solution $u(t,x)$ is called *self-similar* if it is invariant under the natural scaling symmetry of the equation, and *weakly localized* if it is not asymptotically free yet does not remain confined to any bounded region — instead spreading slowly so that its $L^2$-mass on every compact set tends to zero while the global $L^2$-norm stays bounded away from zero.

Address the following in space dimensions $d < 5$:

1. Construct stable self-similar weakly localized solutions to such mass-critical (suitably saturated) dispersive or hyperbolic equations in dimensions $d \in \{1,2,3,4\}$, including, where possible, the spherically symmetric setting in $d \geq 3$.

2. Prove that for a suitable class of global solutions (for instance, spherically symmetric finite-energy solutions in $d \geq 3$), the asymptotic decomposition
$$u(t) = u_{\text{free}}(t) + w(t) + o_{L^2}(1) \qquad \text{as } t \to \infty,$$
holds, where $u_{\text{free}}$ solves the corresponding linear equation and $w$ is weakly localized, and rule out collapse to a purely localized state (i.e. show $u_{\text{free}} \not\equiv 0$ for a generic/relevant class of data).

3. Determine whether such weakly localized components can occur for systems of equations and whether their existence is compatible with, or violates, the inverse-scattering principle that the asymptotic (scattering) data uniquely determine the solution.
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of stable self-similar weakly localized solutions is currently established only in dimensions $\geq 5$, and extending it to lower dimensions, together with the corresponding free-wave-plus-weakly-localized decomposition, is listed as an open direction. Recent work (e.g., 2025 preprints on small-amplitude self-similar solutions for one-dimensional dispersive models such as mKdV, quartic KdV, and cubic NLS) provides partial progress on related self-similar structures, but no full resolution in dimensions $d<5$ for the stable weakly-localized scenario or the non-collapse statement is reported.

status_evidence.title: A new paradigm for scattering theory of linear and nonlinear waves: review and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: current method of construction applies only in five or more dimensions ... it is anticipated that similar results hold in any dimension ... one must demonstrate that certain solutions do not collapse to a purely localized form
status_evidence.claim: Construction is presently restricted to dimensions ≥ 5 and the lower-dimensional case, together with the non-collapse statement, is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Small-Amplitude Self-Similar Solutions for one-dimensional Nonlinear Dispersive Equations
status_evidence.snippet: systematic approach for the construction of small-amplitude self-similar solutions ... applied to ... modified Benjamin-Ono, quartic KdV and cubic NLS
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress exists for self-similar solutions in one space dimension, but does not address the stable weakly localized decomposition for mass-critical models in d<5.
